'''800''' ('''eight hundred''') is the [[natural number]] following [[700 (number)#790s|799]] and preceding [[801 (number)|801]].

== In mathematics ==
It is the sum of four consecutive primes (193 + 197 + 199 + 211). It is a [[Harshad number]], an [[Achilles number]] and the area of a [[square]] with diagonal 40.<ref name="area of a square with diagonal 2n">{{cite OEIS|A001105|2=a(n) = 2*n^2}}</ref>

== Integers from 801 to 899 ==

=== 800s ===

==== 801 ====
801 is a [[Harshad number]]. 801 is the sum of a square and positive cube in more than one way, and a sum of distinct positive cubes in more than one way:<ref>{{Cite OEIS|sequencenumber=A003998|name=Numbers that are a sum of distinct positive cubes in more than one way}}</ref><ref>{{Cite OEIS|sequencenumber=A055393|name=Sum of a square and a nonnegative cube in more than one way}}</ref>

: <math>801 = 17^2 + 8^3 = 26^2 + 5^3 = 1^3 + 2^3 + 4^3 + 6^3 + 8^3 = 2^3 + 4^3 + 9^3.</math>

In the [[gematria]] of 2nd century bishop [[Irenaeus]], 801 stands for both the [[Greek language|Greek]] word for a dove, and for [[Alpha and Omega]], and therefore represents God in two ways.<ref>{{citation|title=The Greek Qabalah: Alphabetical Mysticism and Numerology in the Ancient World|first=Kieren|last=Barry|publisher=Weiser Books|year=1999|isbn=9781609252274|pages=110–111|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=w70rWN_-ANAC&pg=PA110}}.</ref>

There are 801 club patterns in a 50x50 grid of coins.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A229093 - OEIS|url=https://oeis.org/A229093|access-date=2026-06-15|website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 802 ====
802 = 2 × 401. It is a [[nontotient]], a [[happy number]], the sum of eight consecutive primes (83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113), and the sum of 4 consecutive triangular numbers<ref>{{OEIS|A005893}}</ref> (171 + 190 + 210 + 231).

==== 803 ====
803 = 11 × 73. It is a Harshad number, the sum of three consecutive primes (263 + 269 + 271), and the sum of nine consecutive primes (71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107).

There are 803 partitions of 34 into Fibonacci parts.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A003107|Number of partitions of n into Fibonacci parts (with a single type of 1)|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 804 ====
804 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 67. It is a nontotient, a Harshad number, and a [[refactorable number]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A174457|Infinitely refactorable numbers|access-date=2023-10-16}}</ref>

"The 804" is a local nickname for the [[Greater Richmond Region]] of the U.S. state of [[Virginia]], derived from [[Area code 804|its telephone area code]] (although the area code covers a larger area).<ref>{{cite newspaper|title=Richmond is getting a new area code. Not everyone is thrilled: 'I’ll be 804 forever'|url=https://www.wtvr.com/news/local-news/new-richmond-area-code-jan-02-2024|newspaper=WTVR-TV|access-date=2025-03-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite newspaper|title=The 804 is running out of numbers|url=https://www.axios.com/local/richmond/2022/07/18/richmond-804-area-code-running-out-of-numbers|newspaper=AXIOS Richmond|access-date=2025-03-16|author=Karri Peifer}}</ref>

==== 805 ====
805 = 5 × 7 × 23. It is a [[sphenic number]]. There are 805 partitions of 38 into nonprime parts<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002095|Number of partitions of n into nonprime parts|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 806 ====
806 = 2 × 13 × 31. It is a [[sphenic number]], a nontotient, a [[happy number]], and the totient sum for first 51 integers.

806 = Phi(51)<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002088|name=Sum of totient function: a(n) = Sum_{k=1..n} phi(k), cf. A000010|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 807 ====
807 = 3 × 269 = antisigma(42)<ref>{{cite OEIS|A024816|Antisigma(n): Sum of the numbers less than n that do not divide n|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 808 ====
808 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 101. It is a [[refactorable number]] and a [[strobogrammatic number]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite OEIS|1=A000787|2=Strobogrammatic numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>
==== 809 ====
809 is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A005384|2=Sophie Germain primes|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[Chen prime]], and an [[Eisenstein prime]] with no imaginary part.
=== 810s ===

==== 810 ====
810 = 2 × 3<sup>4</sup> × 5. It is a harshad number. There are 810 non-equivalent ways of expressing 100,000 as the sum of two prime numbers.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A065577|2=Number of Goldbach partitions of 10^n|access-date=2023-08-31}}</ref> There are 810 distinct reduced words of length 5 in the Coxeter group of "Apollonian reflections" in three dimensions.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A154638|a(n) is the number of distinct reduced words of length n in the Coxeter group of "Apollonian reflections" in three dimensions|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 811 ====
{{redirect-multi|1|811 (number)|the phone number|8-1-1|other topics|811 (disambiguation)}}811 is a prime number, a twin prime, a Chen prime, the largest [[Minimal prime (recreational mathematics)|minimal prime]] in base 9, and the sum of five consecutive primes (151 + 157 + 163 + 167 + 173). It is a [[happy number]] and a zero of [[Mertens function]].

==== 812 ====
812 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 7 × 29. It is an [[oeis:A111592|admirable number]], a [[pronic number]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite OEIS|1=A002378|2=Oblong (or promic, pronic, or heteromecic) numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a balanced number,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A020492|Balanced numbers: numbers k such that phi(k) (A000010) divides sigma(k) (A000203)}}</ref> and a zero of Mertens function.

==== 813 ====
813 = 3 × 271. It is a [[Blum integer]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A016105 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A016105 |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 814 ====
814 = 2 × 11 × 37. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, and a zero of Mertens function. There are 814 fixed [[polyhex (mathematics)|hexahexes]].

==== 815 ====
815 = 5 × 163.  There are 815 graphs with 8 vertices and a distinguished bipartite block.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A049312|Number of graphs with a distinguished bipartite block, by number of vertices|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 816 ====
816 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 3 × 17. It is a [[tetrahedral number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000292|2=Tetrahedral numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[Padovan sequence|Padovan number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000931|2=Padovan sequence|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a Zuckerman number.

==== 817 ====
817 = 19 × 43. It is a [[centered hexagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A003215|2=Hex (or centered hexagonal) numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and the sum of three consecutive primes (269 + 271 + 277).

==== 818 ====
818 = 2 × 409. It is a nontotient and a [[strobogrammatic number]]<ref name=":0" />

==== 819 ====
819 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 7 × 13. It is a [[square pyramidal number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000330|2=Square pyramidal numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

=== 820s ===

==== 820 ====
820 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 41. It is a Harshad number, a [[happy number]], a repdigit (1111) in base 9, and the 40th [[triangular number]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite OEIS|1=A000217|2=Triangular numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 821 ====
821 is a prime number, a [[twin prime]], a Chen prime, and an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part. It forms a [[prime quadruplet]] with 823, 827, and 829. It is a lazy caterer number.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000124 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000124 |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 822 ====
822 = 2 × 3 × 137. It is a sphenic number, a member of the [[Mian–Chowla sequence]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A005282|2=Mian-Chowla sequence|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and the sum of twelve consecutive primes (43 + 47 + 53 + 59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97).

==== 823 ====
823 is a prime number, a [[twin prime]], and a [[lucky prime]]. It forms a prime quadruplet with 821, 827, and 829. It is a zero of Mertens function.

==== 824 ====
824 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 103, [[refactorable number]], nontotient, a zero of Mertens function, and the sum of ten consecutive primes (61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103).

==== 825 ====
825 = 3 × 5<sup>2</sup> × 11. It is a [[Smith number]],<ref name=":3">{{Cite OEIS|1=A006753|2=Smith numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Harshad number, and a zero of Mertens function.

==== 826 ====
826 = 2 × 7 × 59. It is a sphenic number. There are 825 partitions of 29 into parts each of which is used a different number of times.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A098859|Number of partitions of n into parts each of which is used a different number of times|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 827 ====
827 is a prime number, a [[twin prime]], a Chen prime, a Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and the sum of seven consecutive primes (103 + 107 + 109 + 113 + 127 + 131 + 137). It forms a prime quadruplet with 821, 823, and 829. It is a strictly non-palindromic number.<ref name=":4">{{Cite OEIS|1=A016038|2=Strictly non-palindromic numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 828 ====
828 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup> × 23. It is a Harshad number and a triangular matchstick number.<ref>{{OEIS|A045943|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

==== 829 ====
829 is a prime number, a [[twin prime]], a Chen prime, and the sum of three consecutive primes (271 + 277 + 281). It forms a prime quadruplet with 821, 823, and 827. It is a [[centered triangular number]].
=== 830s ===

==== 830 ====
830 = 2 × 5 × 83. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, the totient sum of the first 52 integers, and the sum of four consecutive primes (197 + 199 + 211 + 223).

==== 831 ====
831 = 3 × 277. There are 831 partitions of 32 into at most 5 parts.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A001401|Number of partitions of n into at most 5 parts|access-date=2022-05-25}}</ref>

==== 832 ====
832 = 2<sup>6</sup> × 13. It is a Harshad number and a member of the Horadam sequence (0,1,4,2).<ref>{{OEIS|A085449}}</ref>

==== 833 ====
833 = 7<sup>2</sup> × 17. It is an [[octagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000567 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000567 |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=oeis.org}}</ref> and a [[centered octahedral number]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A001845|Centered octahedral numbers (crystal ball sequence for cubic lattice)|access-date=2022-06-02}}</ref>

==== 834 ====
834 = 2 × 3 × 139. It is a [[cake number]], a sphenic number, a nontotient, and the sum of six consecutive primes (127 + 131 + 137 + 139 + 149 + 151).

==== 835 ====
835 = 5 × 167. It is a [[Motzkin number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A001006|2=Motzkin numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 836 ====
{{main|836 (number)}}

==== 837 ====
837 = 3<sup>3</sup> × 31. It is the 36th generalized heptagonal number.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A085787|2=Generalized heptagonal numbers: m*(5*m – 3)/2, m = 0, +-1, +-2 +-3, ...|access-date=2022-05-30}}</ref>

==== 838 ====
838 = 2 × 419. It is a palindromic number. There are 838 distinct products ijk with 1 <= i<j<k <= 23.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A027430|2=Number of distinct products ijk with 1 <= i<j<k <= n}}</ref>

==== 839 ====
839 is a prime number, a [[safe prime]],<ref name=":5">{{Cite OEIS|1=A005385|2=Safe primes|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and the sum of five consecutive primes (157 + 163 + 167 + 173 + 179). It is a [[highly cototient number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A100827|2=Highly cototient numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

=== 840s ===

==== 840 ====
{{Main|840 (number)}}
==== 841 ====
841 = 29<sup>2</sup> = 20<sup>2</sup> + 21<sup>2</sup>, sum of three consecutive primes (277 + 281 + 283), sum of nine consecutive primes (73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109), [[centered square number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A001844|2=Centered square numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> [[centered heptagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A069099|2=Centered heptagonal numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> [[centered octagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A016754|2=Odd squares: a(n) = (2n+1)^2. Also centered octagonal numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 842 ====
842 = 2 × 421. It is a nontotient. There are 842 series-reduced trees with 18 nodes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000014|Number of series-reduced trees with n nodes}}</ref> 

842!! - 1 is prime.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A007749|Numbers k such that k!! - 1 is prime|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 843 ====
843 = 3 × 281. It is a [[Lucas number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000032|2=Lucas numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 844 ====
844 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 211. It is a nontotient. It is the smallest 5 consecutive integers which are not squarefree:

844 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 211, 845 = 5 × 13<sup>2</sup>, 846 = 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> × 47, 847 = 7 × 11<sup>2</sup>, and 848 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 53.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A045882|Smallest term of first run of (at least) n consecutive integers which are not squarefree|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 845 ====
845 = 5 × 13<sup>2</sup>. It is a concentric pentagonal number.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A032527|Concentric pentagonal numbers: floor( 5*n^2 / 4 )|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>There are 845 emergent parts in all partitions of 22.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A182699|Number of emergent parts in all partitions of n|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 846 ====
846 = 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> × 47. It is a nontotient, a Harshad number, and the sum of eight consecutive primes (89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113 + 127).

==== 847 ====
847 = 7 × 11<sup>2</sup>. It is a [[happy number]]. There are 847 partitions of 29 that do not contain 1 as a part.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002865|Number of partitions of n that do not contain 1 as a part|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 848 ====
848 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 53. It is an [[untouchable number]].

==== 849 ====
849 = 3 × 283, It is a zero of Mertens function and a [[Blum integer]].
=== 850s ===

==== 850 ====
850 = 2 × 5<sup>2</sup> × 17. It is a zero of Mertens function and a nontotient. The sum of the squares of the divisors of 26 is 850 {{OEIS|id=A001157}}. 

The maximum possible [[Credit score (United States)#Range of scores|Fair Isaac credit score]] is 850.

==== 851 ====
851 = 23 × 37 There are 851 compositions of 18 into distinct parts<ref>{{cite OEIS|A032020|Number of compositions (ordered partitions) of n into distinct parts|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 852 ====
852 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 71. It is a [[pentagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000326|2=Pentagonal numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a Smith number.<ref name=":3" />

==== 853 ====
853 is a prime number, a [[Perrin number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A001608|2=Perrin sequence|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a zero of [[Mertens function]], and a strictly non-palindromic number. The average of first 853 prime numbers is an integer {{OEIS|id=A045345}}.  There are 853 connected graphs with 7 nodes.

==== 854 ====
854 = 2 × 7 × 61. It is a [[sphenic number]] and a nontotient. There are 854 unlabeled planar trees with 11 nodes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A002995|Number of unlabeled planar trees (also called plane trees) with n nodes|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 855 ====
855 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 19. It is a [[decagonal number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A001107|2=10-gonal (or decagonal) numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a [[centered cube number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A005898|2=Centered cube numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 856 ====
856 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 107. It is a [[nonagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A001106|2=9-gonal (or enneagonal or nonagonal) numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a [[centered pentagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A005891|2=Centered pentagonal numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a [[refactorable number]].

==== 857 ====
857 is a prime number, a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and the sum of three consecutive primes (281 + 283 + 293).

==== 858 ====
858 = 2 × 3 × 11 × 13. It is a [[Giuga number]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A007850|2=Giuga numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref>

==== 859 ====
859 is a prime number and a [[oeis:A006450|prime index prime]]. There are 859 planar partitions of 11.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000219|Number of planar partitions (or plane partitions) of n|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

=== 860s ===

==== 860 ====
860 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 43. It is aHoax number<ref>{{cite OEIS|A019506|Hoax numbers|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref> and the sum of four consecutive primes (199 + 211 + 223 + 227).

==== 861 ====
861 = 3 × 7 × 41. It is a sphenic number, a [[hexagonal number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000384|2=Hexagonal numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Smith number,<ref name=":3" /> and the 41st [[triangular number]].<ref name=":2" /> 

==== 862 ====
862 = 2 × 431. It is a [[Lazy caterer's sequence|lazy caterer number]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=A000124 - OEIS |url=https://oeis.org/A000124 |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 863 ====
863 is a prime number, a safe prime,<ref name=":5" /> a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and an index of a prime Lucas number.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A001606|Indices of prime Lucas numbers}}</ref>It is the sum of five consecutive primes (163 + 167 + 173 + 179 + 181) and the sum of seven consecutive primes (107 + 109 + 113 + 127 + 131 + 137 + 139).

==== 864 ====
864 = 2<sup>5</sup> × 3<sup>3</sup>. It is an [[Achilles number]] and a Harshad number. It the  sum of a twin prime pair (431 + 433) and the sum of six consecutive primes (131 + 137 + 139 + 149 + 151 + 157).

==== 865 ====
865 = 5 × 173.

==== 866 ====
866 = 2 × 433. It is a nontotient and the [[oeis:A005897|number of cubes of edge length 1 required to make a hollow cube of edge length 13]]. There are 866 one-sided [[polyiamond|noniamonds]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A006534|access-date=2022-05-10}}</ref>

==== 867 ====
867 = 3 × 17<sup>2</sup>. There are 867 5-chromatic simple graphs on 8 nodes.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A076281|Number of 5-chromatic (i.e., chromatic number equals 5) simple graphs on n nodes|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref>

==== 868 ====
868 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 7 × 31 = [[Jordan's totient function|J<sub>3</sub>(10)]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|A059376|Jordan function J_3(n)|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref> It is a nontotient.

==== 869 ====
869 = 11 × 79. It is a zero of Mertens function.

=== 870s ===

==== 870 ====
870 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 29. It is a pronic number,<ref name=":1" /> a nontotient, a sparsely totient number,<ref name=":6">{{Cite OEIS|1=A036913|2=Sparsely totient numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> a Harshad number, and the sum of ten consecutive primes (67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107). It is the [[magic constant]] of ''n''×''n'' normal [[magic square]] and [[Eight queens puzzle|''n''-queens problem]] for&nbsp;''n''&nbsp;=&nbsp;12.

==== 871 ====
871 = 13 × 67. It is the thirteenth [[polygonal number|tridecagonal number]].

==== 872 ====
872 = 2<sup>3</sup> × 109. It is a [[refactorable number]] and anontotient.

872! + 1 is [[Factorial prime|prime]].

==== 873 ====
873 = 3<sup>2</sup> × 97 = 1! + 2! + 3! + 4! + 5! + 6!.

==== 874 ====
874 = 2 × 19 × 23 = 0! + 1! + 2! + 3! + 4! + 5! + 6!. It is a [[sphenic number]], a nontotient, a Harshad number, a [[happy number]], and the sum of the first twenty-three primes.

==== 875 ====
875 = 5<sup>3</sup> × 7. It can be uniquely expressed as a difference of two positive cubes: 875 = 10<sup>3</sup> – 5<sup>3</sup>.<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A014439|2=Differences between two positive cubes in exactly 1 way.|access-date=2019-08-18}}</ref>

==== 876 ====
876 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 73. It is a generalized pentagonal number.<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A001318|2=Generalized pentagonal numbers.|access-date=2019-08-26}}</ref>

==== 877 ====
877 is a prime number, a [[oeis:A006450|prime index prime]], a Chen prime, a zero of Mertens function, a [[Bell number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A000110|2=Bell or exponential numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a strictly non-palindromic number.<ref name=":4" />

==== 878 ====
878 = 2 × 439. It is a  nontotient. There are 878 Pythagorean triples with a hypotenuse less than 1000.<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A101929|2=Number of Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse < 10^n.|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref>

==== 879 ====
879 = 3 × 293. It is a candidate [[Lychrel number|Lychrel]] seed number. There are 879 [[hypergraph#Symmetric hypergraphs|regular hypergraphs]] spanning 4 vertices.<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A319190|2=Number of regular hypergraphs|access-date=2019-08-18}}</ref> 

=== 880s ===

==== 880 ====
880 = 2<sup>4</sup> × 5 × 11 = [[Double factorial#Generalizations|11!!!]].<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A007661|2=Triple factorial numbers|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref> It is a Harshad number and a 148-[[polygonal number|gonal number]]. There are 880 ''n''×''n'' [[magic square]]s for n = 4.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sloane's A006052 : Number of magic squares of order n composed of the numbers from 1 to n^2, counted up to rotations and reflections|url=https://oeis.org/A006052|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-02}}</ref>

==== 881 ====
881 is a prime number, a [[twin prime]], a Chen prime, an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part, and the sum of nine consecutive primes (79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103 + 107 + 109 + 113). It is a [[happy number]].

881 is a bilingual play on words when text chatting in Mandarin Chinese or bilingually Mandarin Chinese and English. "881" is pronounced ''ba ba yi'' in Mandarin, and thus puns on "bye-bye." Probably an elaboration of the similar pun on "88" (''ba-ba''). See [[88 (number)]].{{Citation needed|date=August 2021}}

==== 882 ====
882 = 2 × 3<sup>2</sup> × 7<sup>2</sup> = <math>\binom{9}{5}_2</math> It is a [[trinomial triangle|trinomial coefficient]],<ref>{{cite OEIS|1=A111808|2=Left half of trinomial triangle (A027907), triangle read by rows|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref> a Harshad number, and the totient sum of the first 53 integers.

==== 883 ====
883 is a prime number, a [[twin prime]], a lucky prime, the sum of three consecutive primes (283 + 293 + 307), and the sum of eleven consecutive primes (59 + 61 + 67 + 71 + 73 + 79 + 83 + 89 + 97 + 101 + 103). It is a zero of Mertens function.

==== 884 ====
884 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 13 × 17. It is a zero of Mertens function. There are 884 points on surface of tetrahedron with sidelength 21.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A005893|2=Number of points on surface of tetrahedron|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref>

==== 885 ====
885 = 3 × 5 × 59. It is a [[sphenic number]]. There are 885 series-reduced rooted trees whose leaves are integer partitions whose multiset union is an integer partition of 7.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A319312|2=Number of series-reduced rooted trees whose leaves are integer partitions whose multiset union is an integer partition of n|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref>

==== 886 ====
886 = 2 × 443. It is a zero of Mertens function.

==== 887 ====
887 is a prime number followed by primal [[prime gap|gap]] of 20, a safe prime,<ref name=":5" /> a Chen prime, and an Eisenstein prime with no imaginary part. It is the first iteration of the [[Lychrel number|196 trajectory]] (196 + 691 = 887).

==== 888 ====
{{Main|888 (number)}}

==== 889 ====
889 = 7 × 127. It is a zero of Mertens function.

=== 890s ===

==== 890 ====
890 = 2 × 5 × 89. It is a sphenic number, a nontotient, and the sum of four consecutive primes (211 + 223 + 227 + 229). 890 is the sum of the squares of two successive primes: 890 = 19<sup>2</sup> + 23<sup>2</sup>.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A069484|2=a(n) = prime(n+1)^2 + prime(n)^2.|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref> 

==== 891 ====
891 = 3<sup>4</sup> × 11. It is an [[octahedral number]] and the sum of five consecutive primes (167 + 173 + 179 + 181 + 191).

==== 892 ====
892 = 2<sup>2</sup> × 223. It is a nontotient. There are 892 regions formed by drawing the line segments connecting any two perimeter points of a 6 times 2 grid of squares like [[oeis:A331452/a331452_16.png|this]] {{OEIS|id=A331452}}.

==== 893 ====
893 = 19 × 47. It is a zero of Mertens function.

893 is considered an unlucky number in [[Japan]], because its digits read sequentially are the literal translation of ''[[yakuza]]''.

==== 894 ====
894 = 2 × 3 × 149. It is a sphenic number and a nontotient.

==== 895 ====
895 = 5 × 179. It is a Smith number,<ref name=":3" /> a [[Woodall number]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A003261|2=Woodall numbers|access-date=2016-06-11}}</ref> and a zero of Mertens function.

==== 896 ====
896 = 2<sup>7</sup> × 7. It is a [[refactorable number]], a zero of Mertens function, and the sum of six consecutive primes (137 + 139 + 149 + 151 + 157 + 163).

==== 897 ====
897 = 3 × 13 × 23. It is a sphenic number and a Cullen number {{OEIS|id=A002064}}.

==== 898 ====
898 = 2 × 449. It is a nontotient and a zero of Mertens function.

==== 899 ====
899 = 29 × 31. It is the product of a pair of [[twin prime|twin primes]],<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=A037074|2=Numbers that are the product of a pair of twin primes|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref> a [[happy number]], and the smallest number with digit sum 26.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|1=
A051885|2=Smallest number whose sum of digits is n|access-date=2022-05-11}}</ref> There are 899 [[oeis:A000607|partitions of 51 into prime parts]].
